tasks.notes: fleet/run-engine.mjs: the dispatch snapshot is taken at a later instant than the head it claims to describe, so it can name a sibling whose work is not in the tree the worker was handed — the exact case M1 exists to re-edge. In `dispatchOnce` `head` is read at the top (`const head = adoptedHead`), but `adoptedAtDispatch.set(task.id, new Set(adoptedIds))` runs only after `await anchorClone(task, head)` (git fetch + detached checkout + `resetTaskClone` + the bootstrap command) and the optional `resetTaskClone` for a re-edged task. `foldEpoch` assigns `adoptedHead = merge.headSha` and `for (const t of epochTasks) adoptedIds.add(t.id)` on adjacent lines, and it runs on another lane under `underFoldLock`, which `anchorClone` does not hold — so a fold completing inside that window adds sibling S to `adoptedIds` while this dispatch's `head` still predates S. The worker is handed `head` (`runTask(task, head, siblingsNow(task))`), which lacks S's work; it returns BLOCKED naming S; `blockingSiblingsOf` reads `adoptedThen`, finds S present, filters it out, and the task ends `failed: not-reviewed` instead of being re-edged. `retryParkedInfra` has the identical skew (`head` at its top, snapshot after `anchorClone` and `resetTaskClone`). The added comment asserts the invariant the placement does not hold: "task id → the ids IN that head". The window is not theoretical — `anchorClone` is seconds of git and bootstrap IO and folds run concurrently on other lanes at width ≥ 2. Fix is to read the set in the same tick as `head`, which is the only instant at which `adoptedHead` and `adoptedIds` are consistent; both sites are inside this task's FILES. The exam does not catch this because (d.5a) adopts A strictly after B's `worker:start` is already on the log, i.e. after the snapshot was taken.
